strings.name: Leonardo da Vinci
strings.summary: Leonardo worked in Florence, Milan and at the French court, influencing European painting through works such as The Last Supper and the Mona Lisa. He applied observation, drawing and experimental thinking to the human body, nature and machinery, leaving extensive manuscripts. Many engineering ideas remained designs, and numerous artworks were unfinished. His importance lies both in his surviving paintings and in his approach to research across disciplines.
strings.coverageNote: Scholars differ over the dates of some works. The Mona Lisa follows the Louvre’s dating of its beginning to around 1503. The historical portrait is an artwork, not a photograph.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Training
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Apprentice in Verrocchio’s workshop in Florence
strings.facts.fact-03.label: Notable works
strings.facts.fact-03.value: Mona Lisa, The Last Supper, Virgin of the Rocks
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Painting and human expression
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: The Last Supper and the Mona Lisa bring together composition, expression and psychological characterization.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Observation and manuscript research
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Used drawings and notes to investigate anatomy, geometry and machinery. Design concepts should not be confused with inventions actually built.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Dies in France
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Died at Clos Lucé near Amboise, leaving his manuscripts and drawings to his pupil Melzi.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Moves to France by invitation
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Accepted an invitation from King Francis I of France and moved to Amboise, continuing artistic and engineering work.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Travels to Rome
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Left Milan to work in Rome under the patronage of Giuliano de’ Medici.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Begins the Mona Lisa
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Began painting the portrait of Lisa Gherardini around this year and continued revising it for many years.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Serves as an architectural and engineering adviser
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Worked for Cesare Borgia on architectural and engineering matters in the Romagna region.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Completes The Last Supper
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Created the mural in the refectory of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan between 1495 and 1498.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Receives the Virgin of the Rocks commission
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Accepted a Milan altarpiece commission with the de Predis brothers; two versions ultimately survived.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Joins the Milanese court
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Went to the court of Ludovico Sforza, working in painting, sculpture, engineering and stage design.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Joins the painters’ guild
strings.timeline.event-09.text: After training in Verrocchio’s workshop, joined the painters’ company of Saint Luke in Florence.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born near Vinci
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Tuscany, spent his early years near home and later went to Florence to study art.
